entry.evidence: their assignment to specific atomic-scale environments is still debated, and two different models have been proposed to interpret the V (OH) stretching spectrum of tourmaline

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML full text (jats_text), checked against the published PDF

steps.action: Pose the open question of how the W(OH) and V(OH) stretching bands of dravite map onto specific local cation environments.
steps.quote: their assignment to specific atomic-scale environments is still debated

steps.action: Take the two published rival models from the literature: the traditional model (frequency set by cations coordinated to each OH) and the YZZ-triplet model (collective response of the three V(OH) of a cluster).
steps.quote: whereas the “YZZ-triplet” model predicts a single V (OH) band for this cluster

steps.action: Derive from molecular-crystal lattice dynamics that a local or collective response depends on the magnitude of the intermolecular coupling relative to the chemically induced perturbation, which makes the coupling the discriminating quantity.
steps.quote: a more collective response is expected when the vibrational coupling is stronger than the perturbation

steps.action: Set up DFT-PBE plane-wave calculations (Quantum ESPRESSO, SG15 ONCV pseudopotentials, 80/480 Ry cutoffs) with linear-response harmonic phonons for rhombohedral, hexagonal and 1×1×2 supercell models.
steps.quote: Relevant properties were obtained using the density functional theory (DFT)

steps.action: Check the relaxed cell parameters of ideal dravite against experimental values (about 1% overestimate, as expected at this level of theory).
steps.quote: overestimate by ∼ 1 % the corresponding experimental values

steps.action: Diagonalize the full dynamical matrix of the primitive rhombohedral cell of ideal dravite, giving one W(OH) mode and A1 plus E V(OH) modes.
steps.quote: leading to four OH stretching modes among a total of 159 vibrational modes

steps.action: Compare a partial dynamical matrix restricted to O and H atoms of the OH groups with the full matrix to show that the OH stretching modes are decoupled from all other modes.
steps.quote: differ by less than 0.15 cm - 1 from those resulting from the full computation

steps.action: Infer the harmonic coupling parameter λ between V(OH) oscillators from the A1–E splitting (about 0.1 cm-1) in a local-mode description and conclude that the OH groups are nearly independent oscillators.
steps.quote: denotes the weakness of the coupling interaction between the V (OH) oscillators in dravite

steps.action: Repeat the analysis in the hexagonal cell to bound inter-cluster coupling (spread ≤1.4 cm-1) and compare partial-matrix and full-matrix results and the k-point grid choice.
steps.quote: They are also within 1.5 cm - 1 from those obtained on the rhombohedral cell using a comparatively denser k -point grid

steps.action: Design disordered models (X vacancy, Z(Mg), Y(Al), Y–Z inversion and combinations) with a homogeneous compensating background, and restrict frequency calculations to the OH groups of the perturbed cluster (partial Hessian, accuracy cited).
steps.quote: this approach makes it possible to disentangle the influence on the OH stretching modes of individual contributions to the chemical disorder

steps.action: Compute W(OH) and V(OH) frequencies for Y(Al) and Z(Mg) substitutions in the 1×1×2 supercell, showing a dominant nearest-neighbour influence and about 3 cm-1 from next-nearest neighbours.
steps.quote: These results attest to a dominant influence of the occupancy of the nearest-neighbor cationic sites

steps.action: Screen Al–Mg inversion configurations energetically in the hexagonal cell and retain only the neighbouring Y–Z inversion (+13.4 kJ mol-1) as plausible at temperatures up to 800 °C.
steps.quote: only the one with a Mg–Al inversion at neighboring Y and Z sites has been found to be energetically competitive

steps.action: Compute supercell frequencies for the retained inversion and for X-vacancy models (alone and combined with Y(Al) or inversion), finding a 3611 cm-1 V(OH) and downshifts of about 80–100 cm-1 for W(OH) next to vacancies.
steps.quote: In contrast, the frequency of the V (OH) group in a Y Al Z Mg Z Al environment is calculated at 3611 cm - 1

steps.action: Compare hexagonal-cell and 1×1×2 supercell frequencies for the same configurations; most agree within ±15 cm-1, but vacancy-bearing models differ by up to 27 cm-1, which reveals an effect of X-vacancy ordering along c.
steps.quote: they suggest that the ordering scheme of X vacancies along the c axis could have a significant effect on the stretching frequencies

steps.action: Fit a linear relation between OH stretching frequency and OH bond length across all models (slope −15447 cm-1 Å-1) and compare the slope with published theoretical values (Hermansson 1993; quartz; corundum).
steps.quote: the OH stretching frequencies in dravite are linearly correlated with the corresponding bond lengths (Fig. 2)

steps.action: Compare the disorder-induced frequency shifts (>20 cm-1) with the inter-oscillator coupling (<1 cm-1), which places dravite in the weak-coupling limit where the response is local.
steps.quote: are significantly stronger than the vibrational coupling between single OH groups ( < 1 cm - 1 )

steps.action: Reject the need for a collective (YZZ-triplet) response of the three V(OH) groups and the mixed-crystal analogy that underpins it.
steps.quote: it does not appear necessary to consider a collective response of all three V (OH) groups belonging to a given 3(YZZ) cluster

steps.action: Retain the traditional model, in which V(OH) frequencies are set by the occupancy of the coordinating sites.
steps.quote: The present theoretical results support a traditional interpretation of observed V (OH) frequencies

steps.action: Estimate the medium-range inhomogeneous broadening (about 15 cm-1) from bond-length departures in ideal local environments, and argue from cited temperature-dependent spectra that homogeneous broadening is minor.
steps.quote: can contribute to the broadening of the OH stretching signals for ∼ 15 cm - 1

steps.action: Compare theoretical W(OH) frequencies with consensus experimental assignments in synthetic dravite EB28 (Berryman et al. 2016) to establish a systematic theory–experiment offset of about 75 cm-1.
steps.quote: which correspond to an upshift of theoretical frequencies with respect to their experimental counterparts amounting to ∼ 75 cm - 1

steps.action: Assuming the offset holds for all environments, assign the dravite W(OH) and V(OH) bands, reassigning the 3620 cm-1 band to V(OH) in a YMgZAlZMg-XNa environment and assigning the V(OH) components.
steps.quote: Assuming that the shift is systematic and holds for the other types of OH environments, the present results support the following assignments.

steps.action: Extend the comparison to synthetic magnesio-foitite MF2 using the hexagonal-cell (concentrated-vacancy) models; vacancy ordering accounts for the absence of the 3640 cm-1 band.
steps.quote: upshift of the W (OH) frequency due the X site vacancy ordering explains why the dravite band at 3640 cm - 1

steps.action: Assign the magnesio-foitite bands (3657, 3619, 3551, 3511, 3459 cm-1) to local environments and compile all proposed assignments in Table 2.
steps.quote: the band at 3551 cm - 1 can be ascribed to V (OH) in a Y Mg Z Al 2 - X □ environment

steps.action: Check the revised assignments against independent cation-distribution estimates (occurrence probabilities from Bosi et al. 2016) and find them more consistent than earlier assignments.
steps.quote: more consistent with a higher occurrence probability of the ideal environment in dravite samples close to end-member compositions

steps.action: Conclude that the traditional local model holds and that X vacancies act on a longer scale, explaining dravite versus Mg-foitite spectral differences.
steps.quote: The present results thus support a traditional interpretative model which assumes that the local environment of a single OH group has a determining influence

Conditions set in silico: site occupancies, vacancies and cell size chosen in the DFT models
Survives partial versus full matrix, k-grid and cell-size variation, and an extension to Mg-foitite spectra
Traditional model kept; collective response not needed; bands reassigned
No review file supplied; not assessable

end.claim: OH stretching in dravite behaves as nearly independent oscillators (coupling below 1 cm-1) whose frequencies are set mainly by the occupancy of the coordinating sites, supporting the traditional model over the YZZ-triplet model, with X vacancies acting over a longer range.

decisive_move.sentence: Inferring the harmonic coupling between V(OH) oscillators from the A1–E splitting (about 0.1 cm-1) is what places dravite in the weak-coupling limit and removes the basis for a collective response.

gates.evidence: The rival local and collective models and the coupling-versus-perturbation criterion are stated before the calculations (§1 ¶4–5) and direct what is computed (coupling λ, disorder shifts). The coupling could have come out comparable to the disorder shifts, which would have favoured the collective model (§4.1 ¶2). Nothing was fixed in advance: model choice and the 75 cm-1 offset were set during the analysis.

imports.item: Density functional theory with the PBE generalized gradient approximation
Quantum ESPRESSO PWscf and PHonon codes with SG15 ONCV norm-conserving pseudopotentials
Linear response (density functional perturbation) theory for harmonic phonons (Baroni et al. 2001)
One-mode and two-mode phonon behaviour of mixed crystals (Chang and Mitra 1971)
Lattice dynamics of molecular crystals: intermolecular coupling as a perturbation of internal vibrations (Califano et al. 1981)
Local mode theory for three equivalent X–H groups in C3v molecules (Halonen and Child 1983)
Frequency–bond-length slope of OH- in an external electric field (Hermansson 1993)

novelty_claims.quote: Based on theoretical stretching frequencies, new interpretations are proposed for some of the bands experimentally observed in synthetic samples of dravite and magnesio-foitite.
Based on the theoretical frequencies, revised interpretations are proposed for some of the W (OH) and V (OH) bands experimentally observed in synthetic [...] .

limits: No peer-review file or discussion was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The acknowledgements mention a review of an initial version by E. Berryman, but what changed is not recorded. The work is purely computational, with no new spectra. Experimental band assignments rest on the assumption that the ~75 cm-1 theory–experiment offset, calibrated on two consensus W(OH) bands, holds for all environments, including V(OH) (§4.2 ¶3–4). Models are at constant volume, use a homogeneous compensating background rather than explicit coupled substitutions, and sample a limited number of configurations (§3.2 ¶1; §4.1 ¶4). For the disordered models, the ~1 cm-1 accuracy of the partial-matrix restriction is assumed from the ideal case, not checked for each model (§3.2 ¶2). How the 'most pertinent configurations' were chosen for supercells is not stated beyond the energetic screen (inference). Neglect of the dravite–Mg-foitite cell contraction is not tested. Sub-claims: the coupling magnitude (<1 cm-1) is estimate_with_resolution; the frequency–bond-length relation across models is regularity_in_range; the medium-range broadening (~15 cm-1) is estimate_with_resolution; the band assignments (Table 2) are best_explanation, conditional on the offset assumption; the X-vacancy ordering effect is best_explanation, suggested by the cell-size comparison.

disagreements.target: YZZ-triplet model of Watenphul et al. (2016), as further used by Bosi et al. (2016)
disagreements.support: The computed inter-oscillator coupling (<1 cm-1) is far smaller than disorder-induced shifts (>20 cm-1), so V(OH) groups respond locally rather than collectively.
disagreements.quote: it does not appear necessary to consider a collective response of all three V (OH) groups belonging to a given 3(YZZ) cluster

disagreements.target: Theoretical basis of the YZZ-triplet model in the mixed-crystal phonon picture (Chang and Mitra 1971, as invoked by Watenphul et [...]
disagreements.support: The authors argue that crystals with molecular units differ from lattice-type mixed crystals, and the DFT results show localized OH stretching rather than a collective lattice response.
disagreements.quote: This behavior differs from that of lattice excitations in mixed crystals, which present a collective response to local mass or force constant variations

disagreements.target: Assignment of the 3620 cm-1 band in synthetic dravite to W(OH) in a YAl2YMg-X□ environment (Berryman et al., 2016)
disagreements.support: Computed frequencies place the YAl2YMg-X□ W(OH) band lower, overlapping the V(OH) band, while a YMgZAlZMg-XNa V(OH) matches 3620 cm-1; Mg-foitite spectra are consistent with this.
disagreements.quote: could however better correspond to V (OH) groups in a Y Mg Z Al Z Mg- X Na environment than to W (OH) groups

disagreements.target: V(OH) band assignments of Berryman et al. (2016) and Bosi et al. (2016) under the traditional approach
disagreements.support: Reassigning the high-frequency V(OH) component to the ideal YMgZAl2-XNa environment matches the expected occurrence probabilities better than the earlier assignment.
disagreements.quote: Although the present assignments (Table 2) partly differ from those previously proposed by Berryman et al. (2016) and Bosi et al. (2016)

disagreements.target: Expected relation between OH stretching frequency and the sum of nearby cationic charges (bond-valence expectation)
disagreements.support: The Mg–Al inversion gives an iso-charge V(OH) environment at 3611 cm-1, well below the 3653 cm-1 of the ideal environment.
disagreements.quote: the expected relation between the OH stretching frequency and the sum of nearby cationic charges is not strictly followed
